title: Parametric Representation of a Translated Circle
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find a set of parametric equations and an appropriate parameter interval to represent a circle of radius r = 5 centered at (2, -3), traversed once counterclockwise starting at (7, -3).

steps.title: Recall the Standard Circular Parametrization
steps.mathExpression: x_0(t) = r\cos t, \quad y_0(t) = r\sin t, \quad t \in [0, 2\pi]
steps.explanation: A circle of radius r centered at the origin starting at (r, 0) and traversed counterclockwise is parametrized by r*cos(t) and r*sin(t).
steps.why: Unit circle coordinates (cos t, sin t) scaled by r trace a circle of radius r counterclockwise.

steps.title: Incorporate the Center Translation
steps.explanation: Adding the coordinates of the center shifts the origin of the circle to (h, k) = (2, -3).
steps.why: Vector translation adds displacement (h, k) to position coordinates.

steps.title: Verify Starting Point and Cartesian Form
steps.explanation: At t = 0, x(0) = 2 + 5(1) = 7 and y(0) = -3 + 5(0) = -3, matching the starting point. Squaring and summing confirms the standard circle equation.
steps.why: Pythagorean identity cos^2(t) + sin^2(t) = 1 confirms the Cartesian radius constraint.
